---
title: "How to compare 3 or more measurements of the same people"
description: "Compare 3 or more measurements taken from the same respondents."
---

Compare 3 or more measurements taken from the same respondents.

The example in this guide is *A 3-day event*. A pre and post training evaluation over 3 days: the same participants rate each day of a training course.

## In SurveyStudio

1. In RStudio, open the **Addins** menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo** and pick `repeated`.
2. On **Design**, see the 3 daily ratings. Each respondent rates every day, so the ratings stay in 1 row.
3. On **Design**, choose **Plan**: repeated-measures ANOVA compares the means, and the Friedman test compares ranks.
4. On **Analyse**, run the plan and read the assumption notes before choosing which test to report.

## In R

```r
d <- sframe_demo("repeated")
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
```

## The research questions and what the report gives

| Research question | Method | What the report gives |
|---|---|---|
| Did ratings change across the 3 days? | Repeated measures ANOVA | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |
| Did ratings change across the 3 days, without assuming normality? | Friedman test | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |

Run the example in SurveyStudio or R to see the results, each marked as demonstration data.
